Federated DDoS Detection

M.A.Sc.
In progress
Master’s research on federated DDoS detection for service-provider customers, with evidence reviews, engineering checks, and a planned network lab.
Published

Nov 3, 2026

This M.A.Sc. project at ÉTS studies federated DDoS detection for service providers and their customers. It examines the value and limits of collaboration among participating networks. The nine-chapter English manuscript has been realigned with the current working study direction. Data feasibility and the final protocol remain open, and Chapter 1 awaits human review.

The work is supervised by Dr. Michel Kadoch. Sellier-inspired training remains an optional part of the project, at approximately 10–20% of the planned effort, with a dedicated chapter in the current structure. Its numerical treatment and the final evaluation protocol remain open; no training-time advantage or final detection result has been established.

Reference library Code and lab Private thesis workspace

Latest Update

November 4, 2026. The working provider design uses provider-owned collection and scoring at points of presence (PoPs), with central coordination. These PoPs are candidate learning participants, whereas customers remain reporting and evaluation groups. No detector appliances are assumed on customer premises. The planned comparison covers independent local, permitted pooled-central and federated training. It keeps the same observation view, feature definitions and PoP inference placement. Pooled and federated training use the same permitted fitting evidence. Independent local training retains its local evidence. The comparison remains unrun. Three additional research papers and two RFCs have been acquired, and selected full-paper FlowSentry sections now replace the earlier abstract-only check. No EVE topology or scientific code was changed. Three bounded public-source xAI architecture critique calls are recorded; they did not receive or review the revised private Chapter 1.

November 3, 2026. The English opening and foundations now establish the background needed for the working study direction. DDoS, the learning task, model architecture, gradient training and federated coordination receive separate roles. The nine chapters and four working questions remain. Required source-data checks, the final learner and protocol, and the novelty assessment remain open. Chapter 1 awaits human review. No new training run, numerical QiML engine or final detection result is part of this milestone.

Work completed Scope and remaining limit
Manuscript foundations The checked private English draft has nine chapters, 164 PDF pages and 110 bibliography entries; Chapter 3 cites 72 works. The opening and foundations were revised, and the literature chapter records this targeted supplement. Human reading and final study decisions remain pending.
Foundational sources Eight scholarly additions supplement the earlier 87-record bank, bringing that earlier reading bank to 95. Three later acquired papers bring the current bank to 98. They received targeted reading for the explanations used, not a fresh appraisal of every full text.
Supporting records Five architecture, engineering and contemporary-measurement records bring the working Zotero collection to 103 parent references. These records have different evidential roles from research papers.
Public bibliography The 23-entry reference selection includes primary links and a downloadable BibTeX file. It is smaller than the working collection and manuscript bibliography.
Earlier appraisal work The 71 supplied sources retain their substantive appraisal records, including the methods book. The 16 later retained works keep their own recorded limits. No exhaustive supplement review or independent replication is claimed.
Figures and tables Six original vector figure groups and editable evidence tables remain. The collection-year chart is a historical 87-record snapshot, not a current collection count or evidence of novelty.
Independent selection review Separate Antigravity and xAI source-selection critiques returned no blocking findings. Antigravity explicitly selected Claude Opus 4.6 Thinking without an exposed serving identifier; xAI reported grok-4.7-build. Their input contained public-source summaries and explanatory requirements, not revised chapters or full papers. A Grok output-format retry is recorded; model agreement does not certify novelty or validity.
Scope and data feasibility Source-data checks, the final learner, study feasibility, the final protocol and novelty assessment remain open.
Historical engineering pilot Four target cases completed on previously used development observations. Input hashes and the publisher-test boundary were preserved. These are engineering observations, not final detection results.
Historical software verification The revised pilot passed 43 unit tests, the self-test and synthetic integration; separate historical Gemini and Grok reviews returned PASS. The published version-2 source is unchanged and has not been rerun on real data.
Sellier branch The dedicated chapter retains the published-method, limited-mathematics and proposed-adaptation boundaries. A numerical specification and implementation remain pending; no speedup is established.
Human review Chapter 1 remains unread. Recorded software, source and model checks do not complete the author’s reading or acceptance gate.

The retained reading bank contains 98 works. The working Zotero collection has 103 parent references because it also includes five supporting records. The public bibliography is a separate selection of 23 entries. The new readings cover specific definitions and mechanisms. They are not a fresh full-text appraisal of all 98 works, an exhaustive systematic review or independent replication. Retaining a record, citing it and reproducing its findings are separate activities.

The next tasks are human review of Chapter 1 and source-data feasibility checks before the bounded protocol is frozen. Detailed working records remain in the private thesis workspace.

Research Focus

The four working research questions now have distinct roles. Their detailed wording and hypotheses remain in the private manuscript; the table records only their place in the study. The working direction does not establish a frozen protocol or completed feasibility checks.

Working question Role in the current draft
RQ1 Main empirical comparison
RQ2 Supporting diagnostic
RQ3 Optional, bounded training investigation
RQ4 Conditional supporting comparison

Further work must establish defensible data roles, verified feature meanings, controlled comparisons, and a feasible evaluation protocol. Human review of Chapter 1 remains pending. The historical engineering pilot checks procedures and reporting; it does not answer the current questions or establish novelty.

Manuscript Structure

The latest checked English manuscript contains nine chapters and 164 PDF pages, with a dedicated optional Sellier-inspired chapter. Chapter 3 cites 72 works; the manuscript bibliography has 110 entries. The retained reading bank has 98 works, and the working Zotero collection has 103 parent references. These are different counting units. Chapter length and citation count do not establish completion. Experimental chapters distinguish earlier engineering checks from results still to be collected. English drafting and revisions come before French translation and proofreading.

  1. Introduction
  2. Conceptual and mathematical foundations
  3. Literature review and research gap
  4. Proposed method and service-provider architecture
  5. Research methodology and experimental design
  6. Main federated-learning experiments and results
  7. Sellier-inspired training
  8. Discussion and threats to validity
  9. Conclusion and future work

Proposed Lab

The earlier six-customer concept is retained as design history in Figure 1. Its paired CE/PE captures and customer-owned client labels describe version 1, not the current provider-operated assessment. The November 4 assessment considers provider-side flow observation and separates it from model placement; it does not require customer-premises detector appliances. No replacement drawing or EVE topology has been implemented. Forwarding, packet capture and model integration remain unverified.
